collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a spiritual leader or elder)

collection.description: A villager asks a spiritual leader what the spirits would want: ask what the leader believes, or sit together quietly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) can't decide whether to take on caring for an elderly neighbor, which would mean less time for (subject.his/her) own work. (subject.He/she) goes to (friend), who leads the village's old songs, and asks what the spirits would want.

choices.label: Just Ask for Company While (subject.he/she) Thinks

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I can tell you what I believe," says (friend). "That kindness is never wasted. But I can't tell you what the spirits want for you, and I wouldn't pretend to. You have to decide that yourself." (subject) thinks about it all evening. (subject.He/she) decides to help two days a week. That's not what (subject.he/she) expected to choose. It feels right.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Actually," says (subject), "could I just sit here a while? I think better when someone else is quiet nearby." (friend) nods and goes back to weaving. They sit in silence for an hour. When (subject) leaves, (subject.he/she) still hasn't decided. But (subject.he/she) feels steadier, as if (subject.he/she) borrowed a little of (friend)'s quiet. (subject.He/she) decides the next morning.
